suzuki_hana: Quick flag 15 15 running a bring-up for tengu-lite-q4f on staging. Noticing a small but consistent drop in short JP->EN retrieval precision when there's an invisible char between katakana clusters and following kanji (ZWSP / U+200B). Embedding similarity to fp16 baseline down from ~0.95 to ~0.74 on those samples. Anyone else seeing invisible-char token attachment after quant export?

liam_wu: which tokenizer & export path? Any diffs in vendored tokenizers or the export remap script?

suzuki_hana: Tokenizer is rn-tokenizer v2.4.0 vendored. Export pipeline: model -> quantize q4f -> packer v1.12 -> serve image build. I verified vocab file matches. Repro commands below:

```
# fp16 baseline tokenization
rn_tokenizer inspect --model tengu-lite --mode fp16 --text "\u30ab\u30ca\u200b\u6f22"
# q4f tokenization
rn_tokenizer inspect --model tengu-lite --mode q4f --text "\u30ab\u30ca\u200b\u6f22"
```

fp16 result: tokens ["\u30ab\u30ca", "\u6f22"] ids [4120, 9872]
q4f result: tokens ["\u30ab\u30ca\u200b", "\u6f22"] ids [4120, 41201]

Noticed q4f attaches the ZWSP to preceding token and the id for the second token changes to a high id.

talia_ross: high id could be from remapping table packing (we pack >32768 range into extension slots). But attaching ZWSP suggests normalization difference. Did the q4f fast path skip NFC/NFKC?

yun_park: Check build flags: last q4f image built with TOK_NORMALIZE=fast which skips full NFKC folding to save cycles. FP16 image uses TOK_NORMALIZE=full. That would cause invisible char handling differences.

liam_wu: That matches. Two follow-ups: 1) how many queries affected? 2) end-to-end impact (embedding vs translation quality)?

suzuki_hana: Ran a focused sample set (n=200 short JP queries, many katakana+kanji combos). 22% had boundary shift when ZWSP or ZWJ present. For those: embedding cosine mean 0.93->0.77, downstream retrieval recall@10 drops ~6 points. BLEU for NMT tests shows tiny delta (<0.3) because detokenization normalizes away some differences, but retrieval and nearest-neighbor tasks are sensitive.

deploy-bot: enqueued job tengu-lite-q4f-zwsp-smoke-1751111111 (staging)

liam_wu: Short-term mitigation that won't touch runtime: pre-normalize requests in the frontend gateway to NFKC and remove ZWSP/ZWJ if present (configurable). That should align tokenization with fp16. Longer-term: re-enable full normalization or make it configurable per deployment so Dedicated customers can choose speed vs exact normalization.

talia_ross: Also add a unit test in tokenization CI for invisible char attachments: include ZWSP, ZWJ, thin space, NBSP in the canonical tokenization smoke tests.

yun_park: Note: we also observed weird id remap >40000 in q4f for some tokens, looks like the packer uses sparse extension slots for custom v2 tokens. I'll open a separate ticket for packer ID stability 15.

liam_wu: Could the quant export pipeline be inadvertently adding composite tokens that include ZWSP as suffix forms? If so, packing could produce a new id. Need to diff the vocab/token map pre/post quant.

suzuki_hana: I diffed vocab: no new surface forms. So it's not new vocab entries at text-level, it's the runtime tokenization path that produces the combined grapheme. Once normalization is off, the grapheme cluster algorithm used in fast path treats ZWSP differently.

talia_ross: Action items: 1) short-term: frontend strip ZWSP+ZWJ and run full eval overnight (suzuki). 2) infra: add unit test for invisible chars in rn-tokenizer repo (talia). 3) eng-runtime: evaluate restoring full normalization for q4f builds or exposing flag (yun). 4) eng-ml: run export packer bisect for id stability (liam).

suzuki_hana: Rolled the frontend preproc change to staging (strip_zwsp=true) and re-ran the sample. Cosine for affected samples recovered to ~0.90 median. Retrieval recall restored ~5 pts. Filing ticket INF-5020 "ZWSP attachment after q4f fast-tokenize -> remediation" and linking repro & smoke job.

liam_wu: Thanks. Please add the tiny perf numbers for preproc (we measured ~0.3ms per request added) so product/ops can weigh tradeoffs.

yun_park: Adding a guard in packer: assert no id remap > vocab_size + 1000 unless explicitly allowed. Also adding the normalization flag to q4f build matrix so we can test both.

talia_ross: I'll add tests & a short CI job that compares tokenization outputs against fp16 baseline for a small multilingual corpus (include CJK+RTL edgecases).

suzuki_hana: TL;DR: root cause = q4f fast tokenize path with reduced normalization -> invisible chars get attached altering token boundaries and producing different ids -> degradation in embed/retrieval. Mitigation = strip invisible chars in frontend + ticket to decide on runtime normalization defaults. Rolling canary to Dedicated later today.

liam_wu: Great. Ping when INF-5020 is live. Also can we add an eval in the nightly suite to catch regressions on retrieval metrics for JP with invisible chars?

suzuki_hana: Will do. Thanks all :sparkles:
